text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- U.S. President Bill Clinton's brief visit to Romania last week has sent a good signal to investors, the newspaper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian brewers say the country's recent admission to CEFTA is a blow to them, unless the government lowers taxes, the newspaper reports.
- A report drafted by the government's reform ministry forecasts an 8.7 percent unemployment rate in the year 2000, the newspaper quotes Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu as saying.
- One of the key points that the IMF review mission due in Bucharest this week will look into is the government's promises to lower profit and wage taxes, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- The Public Works Ministry has submitted to the government a draft proposal on the creation of a mortgage bank to finance housing construction.
- Simona Marinescu, Labour ministry spokeswoman, speaks in an interview about plans to introduce a new pension law.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Grain harvests in central Cluj county have been damaged by plant diseases.
General:
ADEVARUL
- President Emil Constantinescu, visiting Japan to July 16, will seek to attract investors to modernise port and free trade areas, as well as telecommunications.
- Romania and Turkey are producing an armoured personnel carrier (APC), aligned to NATO operation standards, capable of carrying large numbers of soldiers at top speed.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Villages on the western border with Hungary, near Arad and Satu Mare and in southwest Caras Severin have been flooded recently.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Police in the Transylvanian city of Sibiu arrested three high school principals over acccusations of rigging admission exam papers.
- Police are looking for a young man who killed his father, mother and sister in a weekend murder in Bucharest, the newspaper reports.
- The newspaper runs a full-page report on the most polluted areas in Romania.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
